[TODAY] We hit an asteroid. Here's the scar. ☄️

In 2022, NASA's DART spacecraft slammed into Dimorphos, a 151-meter moonlet of the asteroid Didymos, at 6.1 km per second. It shortened the moonlet's orbit by about 33 minutes. Now ESA's Hera has arrived to inspect the result.

The new images show a crater almost as wide as Dimorphos itself, as if one side were flattened. The moonlet now tumbles. Hundreds of boulders, from football to washing-machine size, orbit the pair.

Reality check: the crater's exact size and the boulders' origin still need closer looks. Hera moves in during December, then releases two CubeSats.

Save this if you want to see how we'd deflect a real threat.

[TODAY] A week in orbit, then a borrowed ride. 🚀

On Nov. 24, China's Shenzhou-24 launched two Chinese astronauts and the first Pakistani ever to reach orbit. It is China's first foreign visitor to its Tiangong station.

The visitor stays about a week and runs four experiments picked from over 300 proposals. He then flies home in the older Shenzhou-23 capsule, in the seat of a crewmate who stays on. That astronaut is set to be China's first to spend a year in orbit.

Reality check: the yearlong stay is the plan; it isn't complete yet.

One week or one year in orbit: which would you pick?

[TODAY] Why do December's shooting stars come from rock? ✨

Every year, Earth plows through trails of debris left by objects circling the Sun. Most meteor showers come from comets. The Geminids come from 3200 Phaethon, a rocky asteroid about 5 km (3.17 miles) wide that loops around the Sun every 1.4 years.

Its grains strike our atmosphere at about 22 miles (35 km) per second. They are several times denser than comet dust, part of why Geminids are bright and often yellow. Scientists still debate whether Phaethon is an asteroid or a "rock comet."

Reality check: NASA says expect 40 to 50 meteors an hour under dark skies; 120 needs perfect conditions.

Save this for Dec. 13-14 and let your eyes adjust for 30 minutes.

[TODAY] A giant star swallowed a Sun-like star. 🌟

In our neighbor galaxy Andromeda, astronomers watched a star slightly lighter than the Sun spiral into a bloated supergiant and merge with it. NASA calls it a first of its kind. The giant was about 350 times wider than the Sun and 18,000 times brighter.

Once the smaller star touched the giant's surface, the end came in about seven orbits, or seven years. Other known mergers of smaller stars took thousands. The eruption came in October 2025. The James Webb Space Telescope looked just 47 days after its peak.

Reality check: what the merged star becomes still needs more observations.

[IMAGINE] Up to one million data-center satellites, approved. 🛰️

What is real: on Nov. 25, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission conditionally approved SpaceX's request for up to 1 million satellites that would work as data centers in orbit, between 500 and 1,002 km up. Amazon, Viasat and astronomers had objected over debris and interference.

Reality check: this is a license, not hardware. Plans for satellites above 600 km still need an approved debris plan. Cooling chips in space and cost remain big unknowns. SpaceX gets about seven years to fly its first working satellite.

The speculation: what if some of the computing behind AI moved off Earth?

Computers in orbit: smart move or space clutter? Tell us below.
